question.text: A long straight wire of a circular cross-section with radius ' $a$ ' carries a steady current $I$. The current I is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The plot of magnitude of magnetic field B with distance $r$ from the centre of the wire is given by

solution.text: We know inside the wire $\begin{array}{ll} B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi R^2} \cdot r & (O < r < R) \\ \text { And } B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r} & \text { for }(R < r) \end{array}$
